answer: Require every agent to post a refundable stake before its reputation can influence shared decisions, then slash that stake when an audited task reveals fabricated or colluding identities. A sybil attacker can still create many accounts, but must lock real value behind each one and risks losing it; splitting identities no longer makes influence cheap. For example, a comet-monitoring network might use a reef survey as an independently checked task, while an ember signal helps flag suspiciously coordinated reports for review.
